# Programmable developer documentation

Read-only integration contracts for Programmable Classic and Custom launches.
Start with discovery, select a chain, and read its manifest before using a deployment.

Source repository: https://github.com/programmablehq/Developers
Canonical site: https://developers.programmable.family
Full agent reference: https://developers.programmable.family/llms-full.txt

## Start here

- [Documentation index](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/programmablehq/Developers/main/docs/README.md): Guides grouped by task.
- [Quickstart](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/programmablehq/Developers/main/docs/quickstart.md): First read or stamp verification.
- [Integration status](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/programmablehq/Developers/main/docs/status.md): Chain-specific availability and evidence states.
- [Examples](https://github.com/programmablehq/Developers/tree/main/examples): Runnable read-only consumers.

## By task

- [Robinhood terminal integration](https://developers.programmable.family/robinhood-terminal-indexer): Verify and index chain-4663 Custom stamps.
- [Robinhood guide as Markdown](https://developers.programmable.family/robinhood-terminal-indexer.md): The same maintained guide in plain text.
- [Trading terminals](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/programmablehq/Developers/main/docs/guides/terminals-and-scanners.md): Labels and per-market feature support.
- [Hosted feed integration](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/programmablehq/Developers/main/docs/reference/hosted-feed.md): Complete traversal, retries, durable cursors and partial data.
- [Launch stamp Router](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/programmablehq/Developers/main/docs/reference/launch-stamp.md): Events, getters, runtime bindings, proofs and finalized test vectors.
- [HTTP API](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/programmablehq/Developers/main/docs/reference/http-api.md): Endpoints, fields and compatibility.
- [Platform fees](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/programmablehq/Developers/main/docs/reference/fees.md): Fee scope, accounting and evidence.
- [Protocol fee claim discovery](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/programmablehq/Developers/main/docs/reference/protocol-fee-claims.md): Independent claim eligibility and wallet boundary.
- [Custom Launch V3 profile guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/programmablehq/Developers/main/docs/guides/direct-native-hook-graph-profile-v3.md): Current Ethereum launch contract and detailed admission rules.

## Live discovery

- [Discovery](https://developers.programmable.family/.well-known/programmable.json): Select the chain's manifest and current API pointers.
- [Ethereum manifest](https://developers.programmable.family/api/v2/manifests/1): Chain 1 deployment inventory.
- [Robinhood manifest](https://developers.programmable.family/api/v2/manifests/4663): Chain 4663 deployment inventory.
- Status: `GET /api/v2/status?chainId={chainId}`.
- Launch feed: `GET /api/v2/launches?chainId={chainId}`.
- Launch detail: `GET /api/v2/chains/{chainId}/launches/{launchId}`.
- Token detail: `GET /api/v2/launches/{chainId}/{tokenAddress}`.
- Token list: `GET /api/v2/token-list?chainId={chainId}`.

## Current chain state

Ethereum (`chainId: 1`) publishes Classic and Custom discovery. Custom Launch
API V1 and V2 retain historical reads; authenticated POST is read-only.
V3 profile `3.3.0` accepts fresh submissions under its separate server admission
and wallet-signing contract.

Robinhood (`chainId: 4663`) has live direct-chain Router provenance. Custom V4 and MultiRole use the current product discovery and their own finalized feeds. Module Mode uses its native source contract. The Developer v2 normalized hosted read model is separate and has no public writes; an empty unavailable feed is not authoritative absence. Its historical V4.0 descriptor can remain planned without describing current V4.1 or MultiRole admission.

Read live state instead of inferring availability from a published schema:

- [Robinhood V4 OpenAPI](https://programmable.market/openapi/custom-launch-v4.json)
- [V4 source-verification status](https://programmable.market/schemas/custom-launch/v4/source-verification-status.json)
- [Developer source-verification projection](https://developers.programmable.family/schemas/v2/custom-launch-source-verification-v4.schema.json)
- [Read API OpenAPI](https://developers.programmable.family/openapi/programmable-v2.yaml)
- [Response schemas](https://github.com/programmablehq/Developers/tree/main/schemas/v2)

## Other Robinhood sources

- [Current launch discovery](https://programmable.market/.well-known/programmable.json): V4 profile, client and live readiness.
- [Custom Launch quickstart](https://programmable.market/docs/developers/custom-launch-quickstart): Network and layout selection, API keys and wallet handoff.
- [Module Mode indexing](https://programmable.market/developer-reference/module-mode-indexing): Native launcher events, source versions and module configuration.
- [MultiRole V2](https://programmable.market/developer-reference/robinhood-terminal-indexer#multi-role-v2): Combined roles and its separate finalized projection.

## Consumer rules

1. Resolve deployment identities from the selected chain manifest. Never infer them from token metadata or third-party labels.
2. Public categories are exactly `classic` and `custom`. Custom requires accepted Registry evidence or a consistent canonical Router CustomGraph stamp.
3. Read Router events and proofs at the same canonical finalized block. Check the exact emitter, runtime and immutable bindings; reject copied events.
4. Keep recognized launches visible when metadata, markets or adapters are unavailable. Preserve unknown fields and nulls; do not invent prices, liquidity, fees or execution support.
5. Scope normalized IDs by chain. Scope Router launch IDs by chain and Router. API resource IDs and onchain bytes32 launch IDs are different identifiers.
6. Complete page traversal before committing its durable resume cursor. Preserve API version, chain and filters on every cursor and after request; handle replay and reorgs idempotently.
7. Treat creator metadata, images and links as untrusted display data. A stamp establishes provenance, not safety, an audit or trading support.
8. Keep finality, exact source verification, indexing completeness and public visibility separate. None establishes another or proves fee accrual.
9. The Developer v2 API is read-only. API launch admission is separate; the controller wallet reviews, signs and broadcasts separately.

Use the [full agent reference](https://developers.programmable.family/llms-full.txt)
and the versioned profile guides for authentication, metadata binding, fee policy,
historical profiles and detailed failure handling.
